sections.html:
Speed depends on the route you pick and the condition of the house. Elmira owners usually weigh three paths: a standard listing, a sale on their own, or a cash sale to a buyer who takes the property in its current state.

A listing reaches the widest group of buyers, but it also brings showings, inspections and a lender's appraisal. A cash sale trims those steps, which helps with an inherited house, a vacant property, a rental with problem tenants, or a home needing work the owner cannot afford. Either way, the city and county steps below govern the paperwork.

Elmira is the county seat of Chemung County, in the Southern Tier just north of the Pennsylvania line. Renters and owners are about evenly split, and home values sit far below the New York average. A roof or furnace bill can take a large bite out of a modest sale price, so repairs weigh heavily here.

Expect buyers to compare condition closely and to ask for credits on deferred maintenance. Interstate 86 meets the city at Exit 56, and state routes 13, 14 and 352 converge here. A typical year brings about 38 inches of precipitation and roughly 42 inches of snow, so roof, gutter and heating condition matter.

The city is built almost entirely in the Chemung River flood plain. Public Works lists the Chemung River, Newtown Creek, Diven Creek, Hoffman Creek, Heller Creek and the storm drains as flooding sources, and records floods in 1889, 1902, 1935, 1936, 1946 and 1972.

The June 1972 storm dropped 6.85 inches of rain in two days and damaged or destroyed roughly 5,000 homes. The city has since joined the FEMA Community Rating System, which it says removed 118 properties from the flood plain and saves policyholders 10% on annual flood premiums.

  • Check the FEMA flood zone for the address before you list, so you can answer the first question most buyers ask.
  • Gather any elevation certificate, repair receipts and insurance claim history.
  • Ask the city Public Works office for its flood information packet if a buyer asks about past water.

The city enforces New York State codes, its own Code of Ordinances and a zoning ordinance, and Code Enforcement posts permit forms, fee schedules and complaint tools. A few programs matter most when you sell a rental or an empty house.

  • Rental registration: an ordinance adopted November 23, 2009 requires every rental property in the city to be registered.
  • Rental certification: a companion ordinance of the same date requires certification of rental properties and sets out when certification can be revoked.
  • Vacant buildings: Code Enforcement keeps vacant building registration and exemption forms.
  • Sanitation: city garbage pickup is opt-in, and the Assessor's Office handles opt-in and opt-out forms, so confirm the status with the buyer.

Community Development also runs a Vacant Rental Improvement Program, an owner-occupied housing grant and loan program and a lead hazard reduction program. Buyers of older houses sometimes use these. The city is drawing up a new comprehensive plan called Thrive Elmira, and a zoning update is among its projects, so a buyer planning a change of use should check current rules.

sections.h2: Tax bills, due dates and assessment challenges
sections.html:
Three separate bills apply to a city house. The City of Elmira collects in two installments due May 15 and September 15. The Town and County bill is payable in full from January 1 to March 31. Elmira City School District taxes are paid in two installments due October 31 and March 31.

The city Assessor's Office, at 317 E Church Street, publishes the assessment calendar and is closed on Wednesdays.

  • June 1: taxable status date, valuation date and the deadline to file any exemption.
  • July 1: tentative assessment roll filed.
  • Third Tuesday in July: Grievance Day, 4:00 to 8:00 p.m., before the Board of Assessment Review.
  • August 10: final roll, with 30 days after that for small claims assessment review or certiorari.

STAR and Enhanced STAR run through the state's Homeowner Benefits Portal, not the city office. The Assessor does not hold billing or payment records, so ask the City Chamberlain's Office for a payoff of any unpaid city tax before closing.

The Chemung County Clerk at 210 Lake Street records deeds for Elmira property. The office takes recordings Monday through Friday until 4 p.m., accepts e-recording through approved vendors, and has deeds searchable back to July 31, 1967.

New York charges a transfer tax of $2 for each $500 of consideration, and the seller normally pays it. The seller or the closing attorney files Form TP-584 with the county clerk within 15 days after the deed is delivered. The extra 1% tax on homes of $1 million or more falls on the buyer, and Elmira's median home value is far below that line. For any county tax balance, the Treasurer's Office offers an online tax clearance request.

sections.h2: Preparing an Elmira house for a fast sale
sections.html:
Before you talk to buyers, gather the flood zone, any elevation certificate, your rental registration and certification if the house is a rental, and the latest bills from the city, the county and the school district. Ask the City Chamberlain for a payoff on any unpaid city tax, and the county Treasurer for a tax clearance.

With those papers in hand, a cash buyer can set a price quickly, and your attorney can schedule the deed, the TP-584 return and the payoffs. Title, payoffs and whether anyone lives in the house decide the timeline, so start estate papers or tenant notices as early as you can.

faqs.q: How fast can an Elmira house actually close?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on title, payoffs and whether anyone lives in the house. A sale with clear title and no financing contingency moves fastest, while inherited or tenant-occupied properties can add weeks for estate papers or notices.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my Elmira rental before selling?
faqs.a: The city requires registration and certification of rental properties under ordinances adopted in 2009. Contact Code Enforcement to confirm your status before you list.

faqs.q: Who sets the property tax bill on an Elmira house?
faqs.a: Three bodies bill separately: the City of Elmira, Chemung County with the town, and the Elmira City School District. The Assessor sets the assessment, and billing questions go to the Chamberlain.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Elmira?
faqs.a: The third Tuesday of July, from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. You file the RP-524 form with the Assessor's Office, and the Board of Assessment Review answers by August 10.

faqs.q: Does flood zone status stop a sale in Elmira?
faqs.a: No, but buyers will ask about it. Gather your flood zone, any elevation certificate and your claims history so a buyer can price coverage up front.
